components.name: Local Authenticators in Devices
components.description: Without a configured Identity API, Devices presents this vault's authenticators with Reload directory and a short scope notice: synced passkeys are not physical-device inventory. Existing identity rows retain names, wrapped public references and enabled state, with the same native Passkeys and Agent keys disclosures, enrollment, local sign-in and confirmed revocation controls. Loading and read errors remain distinct from emptiness; an empty directory links to Create a person, and read failures disable credential mutations. Whole-principal removal restores Reload only if the previously focused control disconnected and focus fell to the body; deliberately moved focus is preserved. Reuses incumbent tokens, wrapping actions and teal focus without imagery. This does not establish completion of broader browser IAM.

components.name: Local Requests
components.description: Access Requests uses flat ruled rows and one inline creation or review fieldset. Native fields select an authenticated person/agent, application and exact registered callback, followed by scopes and reason. Failed operations retain drafts; inline output and alerts distinguish results and read failures from emptiness. Pending review names the request and offers authorized-person selection and request-bound passkey approval or denial. Selection resolves current data by ID, removing obsolete decision controls after expiry or external decisions while preserving active focus; removed records restore the connected initiator or Reload when focus is idle. Withdrawal and settled-history removal require confirmation. Requests expire after five minutes; creation grants no access and approval never bypasses policy. Popup application consent creates a transaction-bound request, obtains a fresh request-bound passkey decision, consumes approval once, then issues through the existing PKCE code flow. The binding covers client, callback, scopes, state, nonce, PKCE and agent. Members may consent only to their own bound sign-in; manual and agent requests require an owner/admin, with shared eligibility rules for review controls and enforcement. This documents the connected popup flow, not completed IAM or full validation gates. Reuses existing tokens and wrapping actions without new assets.

components.name: Local Sessions and Grants
components.description: Access Grants reuses this panel in a grant-only variant without requiring Host; Access Sessions retains the combined encrypted sessions-and-grants ledger. Host delegation controls remain independently available when configured. Flat ruled rows show principals, applications, scopes, expiry and exact public record references. Counts are recorded unexpired authority, never live connections; empty counts use a dash. Loading and read errors remain distinct from emptiness. Both variants use the same confirmed revocation: an inline fieldset names the exact record and Cancel receives initial focus. Closing restores the connected source control or Reload after removal only when focus is idle. Native focus scrolling brings confirmation and restored controls into view. Status and errors stay inline; references and mobile actions wrap, and introductory prose keeps the readable measure. Reuses existing tokens.

components.name: Local Agent Keys
components.description: Native Agent keys disclosure inside each Agents row. Flat ES256 key rows show a suffix and enrollment date. Enroll public key reveals a labeled public JWK textarea; failed saves retain its draft and private keys are never requested. Authenticate agent opens a read-only one-use challenge, expiring after two minutes, followed by a Signed challenge field and Verify agent / Close challenge actions. Native fields scroll internally and action rows wrap. Challenge arrival preserves focus moved elsewhere. Machine session status grants neither human approval nor application access; Sign out agent revokes it and read failures report Local session unavailable. Key revocation requires confirmation; Keep restores the revoke control, while form closure or key removal restores the connected initiator or summary only when focus fell to the body. Disabled agents cannot enroll or authenticate but keys remain revocable. This is local agent authentication, not application delegation or complete browser IAM. Reuses existing tokens without raster imagery.

components.name: Local Application Registration
components.description: Shared native Application registration disclosure in Identity → Applications and Access → Policies, using the same encrypted store and role evaluator. Access lists each application name with its stable public ID wrapped beneath it in the existing muted reference style; introductory prose is limited to 62ch. Local policies work without Host. Disabled applications remain visible with disabled editors, and directory read failures disable editing. Saving a changed policy invalidates existing application grants and requires a new sign-in and explicit consent. A labeled organization select, exact callback textarea and space-separated scopes input configure encrypted registration. Roles allowed per scope follows scope names before Save: native member, admin and owner checkboxes wrap on narrow screens and retain Tab/Space behavior. Unchecked roles are denied, including owners; new custom scopes start unchecked. Role choices share retained drafts and encrypted save/reload; explicit sign-in consent remains required. Save and Reload are explicit; loading and read failures never imply absence, and failed saves retain drafts. Removal requires Confirm removal or Keep registration. Keep restores the removal button; save completion restores its connected initiating control only if focus fell to the body, and removal uses the disclosure summary as that fallback. Registration grants no sign-in or resource access and issues no tokens; this record does not establish completion of browser IAM. Its separate consent panel shows the application, requesting origin, exact callback disclosure and scopes. Agent requests add the named agent and enrolled public key reference disclosure, an Approving person selector limited to enabled organization owners/admins, then passkey verification and explicit Allow agent access or Deny. Person consent retains Person and Allow application; connection status and errors remain inline.

components.name: Local Identity Passkeys
components.description: Native Passkeys disclosure in each People row; credentials load on opening and enrollment or Sign in locally loads the human ceremony on action. Local session status shows expiry; Sign out locally revokes the session. Reopening after disclosure closure or navigation validates the stored session. Directory changes, expiry, or revoking its passkey require fresh sign-in. Flat credential rows show a suffix and enrollment date. Revocation requires confirmation; Keep restores its revoke button, and removal restores the summary only if focus fell to the body. Local sign-in grants no application access and does not establish completion of broader IAM.

narrative.overview: OpenSesame is an end-to-end encrypted vault for humans, agents, websites, and developers. Password-manager canon is expressed in OpenSesame navy and teal, with honest cryptographic claims and a keyboard-first vault filesystem.
keyCharacteristics: Master-password gate, no PIN theater, no recovery path
Navy rail, light canvas, teal for exactly one thing: the primary action
List-and-detail spine for the vault; full-width panels for the plane-backed sections
System font stack with no third-party origin

rules.name: The Competitor Marks Rule
rules.body: Match Bitwarden's habits, never its brand.

rules.name: The Honest Crypto Rule
rules.body: Every claim in the interface is one the code makes true.

rules.name: The No-Recovery Rule
rules.body: Never soften the absence of a recovery path.

dos: Do conceal secret values by default and allow copying without revealing.
Do state what a network-backed surface cannot show while offline or unauthenticated.
Do badge sample data on every item and keep removing it to one action.
Do treat a reload re-locking the vault as correct behavior and say so.
donts: Don't add a shortcut around the master password.
Don't put a secret, or a hash of one, on the network.
Don't let prose run the full width of a panel.
